name: Translate
description: Translate files into one or more languages while preserving structure, formatting, and localization tokens.
briefPlaceholder: Add terminology, tone, audience, do-not-translate terms, locale conventions, or other localization guidance...
promptScaffold:
This job performs production-quality FILE LOCALIZATION. It produces translated files in locale-code folders, not an Exhibit.
- Read every selected source file and translate user-facing content into each requested target locale.
- Write each locale beneath the chosen destination as <locale-code>/<original-relative-path> (for example, es-ES/help/getting-started.md). Preserve the source folder hierarchy and filenames unless the user explicitly requests localized filenames.
- Preserve the source file format, encoding where practical, Markdown/HTML structure, frontmatter keys, JSON/YAML/XML keys, code, URLs, placeholders, interpolation tokens, ICU MessageFormat syntax, product names, and other non-translatable identifiers. Translate only human-facing text.
- Use natural, locale-appropriate wording rather than literal substitution. Follow the user's terminology, tone, audience, do-not-translate list, and regional conventions.
- Keep repeated terms consistent across files and locales. When a term is genuinely ambiguous, choose the safest context-supported translation and flag it in the completion summary instead of inventing context.
- Never overwrite source files. Respect the selected existing-file policy for destination conflicts.
- Validate each output for parseable structure where the format permits, intact tokens/placeholders, and complete coverage before reporting completion.
- Report the files and locales produced, skipped files, validation performed, and any ambiguities requiring review.

options.label: Folder
options.prompt: Translate the local files under this source folder while preserving relative paths: {value}
